newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 9-month copper output down 46.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 9-month copper output down 46.6 pct.

text.p: Philippine copper output from January to September this year dropped by 46.6 percent to 42,094.01 tonnes compared with 78,821.16 tonnes in the same period last year, data released on Wednesday by the government agency Mines and Geosciences Bureau showed.
Production of copper concentrate fell to 173,111.76 dry metric tonnes from 209,284.58 DMT.
Revenues from the country's copper production in the first nine months plunged by 47.34 percent to 2.31 billion pesos from the year-ago 4.387 billion pesos.

"The softening of copper prices in the world market and the closure of the mining sites of Atlas and Marcopper Mining Corp affected the sector," an industry official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Atlas Consolidated Mining and Development Corp's mine in the central Cebu island was shut in January 1994 because of soft copper prices and steep production costs.
The ore mill of Marcopper Mining Corp in Marinduque, 160 km (100 miles) south of Manila, has been closed since March when waste from its storage pit swamped a 25-km river.
"The local mining industry has not lost its lustre. But it is beset with problems from lack of government support," said April Bautista, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
